names.name: original face (benlai mianmu 本來面目)

descriptions: Originally pure, originally unborn and undying, originally complete, originally unmoving, able to produce all dharmas (Huineng's words on awakening, Platform Sūtra 4.13).
The one mind of buddhas and beings, without beginning, neither arisen nor ceased, without form, beyond all measure and names (Huangbo, Chuanxin fayao).
Samādhi is its substance and prajñā its function, like lamp and light (Platform Sūtra 7.1).
negations: 'Originally there is not a single thing' (Platform Sūtra 4.11).
'Neither cold nor hot, neither blue nor yellow, not belonging to existence or non-existence' (Huangbo).
relation_to_self: Not something other than one's own mind: 'if deluded, the buddha is a sentient being; if awakened, the sentient being is a buddha' (Dunhuang Platform Sūtra 52.2).
relation_to_world: All dharmas are not apart from the self-nature and are produced by it; mountains, rivers and ordinary activity are its function; the Pure Land is the purified mind.
caveat: Chan does not posit an ultimate as an object or a being; names such as buddha-nature and mind are 'expedient names' to be dropped ('if you meet the Buddha, kill the Buddha'). The tradition would reject reading its buddha-nature as a Vedāntic self; Chan critics of the 'Śreṇika heresy' (Nanyang Huizhong) explicitly reject an eternal mind-nature that leaves the body.

names.name: empty and calm, numinous awareness (gongjeok yeongji 空寂靈知)

descriptions: The mind that is empty and calm yet numinously aware and never obscured is one's original face and the Dharma-seal transmitted by buddhas and patriarchs (Jinul, Susim kyol).
Samādhi is its substance and prajñā its function; calm and always knowing, knowing and always calm (Susim kyol).
negations: It has no form or characteristic, no size, no boundary, no inside or outside, no birth and death (Susim kyol).
relation_to_self: It is the very one who asks the question — the awareness that sees, hears and acts (Susim kyol).
relation_to_world: It is not the physical body; the body is 'provisional, arising and ceasing', while 'one thing is ever numinous, covering heaven and earth' (Susim kyol).
caveat: Jinul's language of numinous awareness follows Zongmi and the Heze line; Korean critics (Seongcheol) held that this 'understanding-awakening' is not final realization. The tradition would reject reading the true mind as an entity separate from phenomena.

descriptions: 'All sentient beings are originally buddhas' (Hakuin, Zazen wasan, opening line).
The buddha-mind is unborn and marvellously illuminating (Bankei).
For Dōgen, 'whole being is buddha-nature' (shitsuu busshō) and impermanence itself is buddha-nature (Shōbōgenzō Busshō).
negations: Not an object that can be grasped by thought; 'not-thinking' (hishiryō) (Fukanzazengi, after Yaoshan).
relation_to_self: The self studied and forgotten: 'to study the buddha-way is to study the self; to study the self is to forget the self' (Genjōkōan).
relation_to_world: The world is not other than buddha-nature: mountains and waters are the sūtras (Sansuikyō); being is time (Uji).
caveat: Japanese Zen masters differ: Rinzai stresses seeing the nature (kenshō), Sōtō the enactment of buddha-nature in practice, Bankei the Unborn already here. None would accept an ultimate apart from practice and daily life.

names.name: the true person of no rank

descriptions: Seen directly in kenshō when the great doubt shatters (Hakuin).
'Beings are originally buddhas, like water and ice' (Zazen wasan).
negations: No-thought; beyond being and non-being (Wumenguan case 1 commentary).
relation_to_self: The seeing nature is one's own; 'this very place is the Lotus Land, this very body the Buddha' (Zazen wasan closing).
relation_to_world: The world seen after kenshō is the Pure Land here; compassion flows as the 'four wisdoms'.
caveat: Rinzai insists the nature must be seen, not merely believed; it criticises the view that sitting in quiet is itself awakening ('dead sitting').

descriptions: 'Whole being is buddha-nature' (Busshō).
Practice and realization are one: sitting is itself the realization of buddhahood (Bendōwa).
negations: Buddha-nature is not a seed awaiting conditions nor a permanent self; impermanence is buddha-nature (Busshō).
relation_to_self: The self forgotten is authenticated by the myriad dharmas (Genjōkōan).
relation_to_world: Mountains, waters, time and all beings are the presencing of buddha-nature.
caveat: Dōgen rejects the 'Śreṇika heresy' of an eternal mind-nature separate from a perishing body (Bendōwa, Sokushin zebutsu); Sōtō would reject reading buddha-nature as a hidden essence.

names.name: Amitābha as one's own mind (yuishin no Mida)

descriptions: The Pure Land is only mind and Amitābha is one's own nature (the Ming Chan–Pure Land formula followed by Ōbaku).
relation_to_self: Amitābha recited and the reciter are not two.
relation_to_world: The Pure Land is not apart from the purified mind.
caveat: Ōbaku holds recitation and Zen to be one; Hakuin's Rinzai criticised this mixture. Low confidence on a specific Ōbaku text stating this.

names.name: true person of no rank (wuwei zhenren 無位真人)
person of the Way who depends on nothing (wuyi daoren 無依道人)

descriptions: 'On the lump of red flesh there is a true person of no rank, always going in and out of the gates of your face' (Linji lu).
'The mind-dharma has no form and pervades the ten directions; in the eye it is called seeing, in the ear hearing…' (Linji lu).
'Only the person of the Way who depends on nothing, listening to the Dharma, is the mother of all buddhas' (Linji lu).
negations: 'What kind of dried shit-stick is the true person of no rank?' (Linji lu) — no fixation even of this.
relation_to_self: It is 'just you, listening to the Dharma right in front of me'.
relation_to_world: Entering all realms — ordinary and holy, pure and defiled — without being defined by them; 'be master wherever you are'.
caveat: Linji denies that any name — buddha, patriarch, bodhi, nirvāṇa — is the reality; they are 'hitching posts for donkeys'. The tradition would reject reifying the true person as a soul.

descriptions: 'The numinous source shines bright and pure; the branch streams flow in the dark' (Cantongqi).
The real and the apparent interpenetrate in five ranks (Dongshan).
negations: 'Holding to phenomena is delusion; merging with principle is not yet awakening' (Cantongqi).
relation_to_self: 'You are not it; it is just you' (Baojing sanmei).
relation_to_world: Principle and phenomena interfuse and yet each abides in its place (huihu / bu huihu).
caveat: Caodong's 'real' is not a separate substance: 'it' and 'you' are neither identical nor two.

descriptions: 'Every day is a good day' (Biyan lu case 6).
negations: 'A dried shit-stick' as reply to 'what is buddha?' (Wumenguan case 21).
relation_to_world: Containing heaven and earth; cutting off the myriad streams; following the waves (the three phrases).
caveat: Yunmen refuses to give the ultimate any description; low confidence in formulating a Yunmen 'view'.

names.name: the original mind shown as a circle (yuanxiang)

descriptions: 'In the ground of true reality not a single dust is accepted; in the gate of the myriad practices not a single dharma is discarded' (Guishan yulu).
negations: The circle-figures are to be burned once understood (Yangshan).
relation_to_world: Principle is realised suddenly; habit energies are removed gradually.
caveat: The circle is a pointer, not the thing (Yangshan burned the book of 97 circles).

descriptions: 'The three realms are only mind; the myriad dharmas are only consciousness' as Fayan's guiding principle (Rentian yanmu).
negations: 'Not knowing is most intimate' (Luohan Guichen to Fayan).
relation_to_world: Every dharma bears the six characteristics of the Huayan teaching, total and particular at once.
caveat: Fayan uses Huayan categories but as Chan pointers.

descriptions: The mind is like a bright mirror on its stand, to be wiped constantly (the verse ascribed to Shenxiu, Platform Sūtra 4.6).
relation_to_self: The pure mind is one's own, obscured by dust.
caveat: This is the Northern view as the Platform Sūtra presents it (an opponent's report); Northern texts themselves (Guanxin lun) are only summarised here from memory.

descriptions: 'Of the empty and calm mind, the numinous knowing is never obscured… the one word knowing is the gate of all wonders' (Zongmi reporting Heze teaching, Chan Preface).
negations: 'The true suchness is without thought' (Xianzong ji).
relation_to_self: It is one's true nature, known whether deluded or awakened.
caveat: Knowing is not discursive cognition; Zongmi insists it is not the same as seeing and hearing.

descriptions: 'The Way needs no cultivation — only do not defile it… the ordinary mind is the Way' (Mazu's sermon, Jingde chuandeng lu juan 28).
'This very mind is buddha' (Mazu to Damei).
relation_to_self: The very one walking, standing, sitting and lying.
relation_to_world: 'All dharmas are mind-dharmas; all names are mind-names' (Mazu).
caveat: Zongmi criticised Hongzhou for equating all activity with buddha-nature; Hongzhou would reject his charge (see dsp:hongzhou-all-activity-buddha-nature).

descriptions: Mind is fundamentally quiescent; 'forgetting feelings' is practice (Zongmi's report).
'The nature of mind is unborn — what need of knowing and seeing?' (Xinming).
negations: 'Originally there is not one dharma — who speaks of cultivation?' (Xinming).
caveat: Known mostly through others' reports; the Xinming and Jueguan lun attributions are disputed. Low confidence.

descriptions: When no thought arises, that itself is seeing the Buddha; no-thought includes precepts, samādhi and wisdom (Lidai fabao ji).
negations: Thought arising is like the back of a mirror, which reflects nothing (Lidai fabao ji, Musang's saying).
caveat: Baotang's own record; Zongmi reported it as rejecting all practice. Moderate-low confidence in the formulation.
